issuer: the Secretary to the Department of Transport and Planning (VicRoads)
note: Read 2026-10-30 from the Victorian Legislation site's authorised Word versions (converted to text, saved beside them). The Road Safety Act 1986 (version 237) grants a driver licence to a person over the age of 18 (s 19(1)) and sets its fee in fee units: 5.59 for a 3-year licence, 7.45 for a 4-year one and 19.15 for a 10-year one (s 21A); the 10-year term is held. The Road Safety (Drivers) Regulations 2019 (version 021, in force 30 September 2026): a first licence under 21 is a P1 probationary licence for one year (reg 50), followed by a P2 probationary licence for 3 years (reg 52(5)), and a full licence is granted when the probationary period ends (reg 49(2)): a full licence is kept from 22. The fee unit's dollar value for 2026-27 (set by the Treasurer under the Monetary Units Act 2004) wasn't read, and VicRoads' fee pages refused the request behind a Cloudflare check, so the fee is null. Victoria's Proof of Age card isn't held.
